k: Five stations: Makkah (in al-Rusaifah), Jeddah (al-Sulaymaniyah), King Abdulaziz International Airport (linked to Terminal {1}), King Abdullah Economic City, and Madinah (in Knowledge Economic City). The Makkah and Madinah stations are not next to the Harams: in a straight line they are about {2} km from the Ka'bah and about {3} km from the Prophet's Mosque, so plan a taxi or bus for the last part. Official {4} journey times: about {5} minutes from the airport to Makkah, about {6} hour {7} minutes from the airport to Madinah, and about {8}¼ hours from Makkah to Madinah. Some trains take longer, so check the time of your own train, and book only on the official Haramain website or app. Going from Madinah to Makkah for Umrah or Hajj? The train does not stop at the miqat. Put on ihram before boarding, and make the intention before the train passes the miqat.

Roads and camps in Mina look very alike. The Ministry of Hajj advises you to save these on your phone and to carry proof of them with you: - Area number, street and camp number - Your camp's gate - The nearest building or landmark - The nearest train station number, if your group uses the Mashaer train - Your group supervisor's name and phone number Also save the camp's location in your phone's map app, and keep your Nusuk card and pilgrim bracelet on you at all times.

Runs only in the Hajj season, between Arafah, Muzdalifah and Mina. It has nine stations, three at each site; the last one is on the {1}th level of the Jamarat facility. It does not run to the Haram or to the hotel districts of Makkah. In Hajj {2} ({3}) it ran for seven days, from {4} Dhul Hijjah to the end of the days of tashriq. Not every pilgrim rides it: the train is used by the groups assigned to it. If your group is one of them, your company tells you your station and times. Keep your train bracelet on your wrist, do not take luggage on board, do not sit or lie down in the stations, and follow your group's train schedule.

Walking from Mina towards Makkah, you meet them in this order: {1}. The small jamrah (as-Sughra, also called the first): the first one after Masjid al-Khayf. {2}. The middle jamrah (al-Wusta). {3}. Jamrat al-Aqabah (al-Kubra, the big one): at the Makkah end of Mina, the last one you reach. On the {4}th you stone only Jamrat al-Aqabah. On the {5}th and {6}th (and the {7}th if you stay) you stone all three, seven pebbles each, in this order: small, middle, then Aqabah.

Your Hajj company moves you between the sites on a fixed plan, by bus or train, and some groups walk to the Jamarat. The Ministry of Hajj tells pilgrims to travel with their group by the designated transport, for example from Arafah to Muzdalifah, and in {1} it asked pilgrims not to walk between the sites at the restricted times. If your group's plan does include walking, these are rough guides at a steady {2} to {3} km an hour. Walking routes are longer than these distances, and crowds and heat slow you down, so allow more time: - Haram to the Jamarat: about {4} km in a straight line; camps at the far (Muzdalifah) end of Mina are about {5} km or more. {6} to {7} hours. - Mina to Arafah: about {8} km, more between camps far apart. {9} to {10} hours or more. - Muzdalifah to the Jamarat: about {11} km from the middle of Muzdalifah; less from its Mina side, more from its Arafah side. {12} to {13} hours. - Arafah to Muzdalifah: about {14} to {15} km. {16} to {17}½ hours. If you walk, the Ministry advises a sun umbrella and comfortable shoes.
